purpose: Bounded Fair Work Commission and Federal Court enforcement case preserving an observed compensation payment, failed reinstatement, worker enforcement action, and subsequent court remedy as separate endpoints.

events.geography: Australia; Meadley v Sort Worx Pty Ltd [2013] FCA 1012, Federal Court Fair Work Division
events.date_precision: Federal Court judgment date; Commission order issued May 2013, payment and non-reinstatement events followed in June-July 2013
events.denominator: One publicly summarized adjudicated enforcement case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official Fair Work Commission case-example page describing the Commission order and Federal Court enforcement outcome
events.missingness: Worker identity is public but personal file, alternative work, household outcome, later job, standardized trust, recurrence, and exit are not retained; payment is reported by the official institutional follow-up rather than independently audited here
events.exposure: The worker was found unfairly dismissed and the Commission ordered reinstatement plus $24,143 in compensation in May 2013
events.alternatives_before_action: The public FWC case example does not report the worker's alternatives, non-use choice, or substitute employment before enforcement
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The employer initially failed to comply with reinstatement and compensation obligations; the worker pursued enforcement after the deadline passed
events.choice_or_response: The worker sought Federal Court orders requiring compliance and penalties after the employer did not reinstate or compensate her by June 2013
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Employer controlled reinstatement and payment execution; the worker controlled enforcement escalation; the Federal Court controlled enforcement orders and penalty
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The official FWC account reports that the company paid the compensation but did not reinstate the worker; the Court awarded a further $15,045 plus interest and imposed a $10,000 penalty
events.immediate_outcome: Verified institutional report of compensation payment without reinstatement, followed by court-enforced additional monetary relief
events.protected_outcome: A monetary remedy was ultimately paid and further monetary relief was ordered; restoration of the original job was not achieved
events.sacrificed_outcome: The worker did not receive reinstatement and the employment relationship or original opportunity remained unrecovered; household and later-career effects are unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: The worker bore enforcement effort and delay; the employer incurred the original payment, additional court-ordered money, and penalty
events.later_outcome: Payment and enforcement are reported, while reinstatement failed; later employment, household recovery, trust, recurrence, switching, and exit remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: The worker attributed the unresolved remedy to employer noncompliance and used court enforcement; this is an observed institutional-action signal, not a standardized trust measure
events.public_or_collective_response: Individual enforcement through the Federal Court is observed; no later collective or political response is reported
events.counterexample: A remedy can be paid while the principal access remedy—reinstatement—fails, showing that monetary receipt is not equivalent to restored opportunity or recovery
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official Fair Work Commission case-example page, https://www.fwc.gov.au/role-court-unfair-dismissal-cases, summarizing Meadley v Sort Worx Pty Ltd [2013] FCA 1012; the page reports payment and failed reinstatement but is not a payment-instrument audit or claimant follow-up

arrows.evidence: The official FWC case example reports that by June the company had not reinstated or compensated the worker
arrows.counterexample: An order and deadline do not guarantee implementation
arrows.remaining_gap: Exact compliance dates, worker effort, and interim household effects

arrows.evidence: The FWC account reports that the worker sought Federal Court orders requiring compliance and penalties
arrows.counterexample: Court enforcement is a visible action route, not evidence that all workers can access it
arrows.remaining_gap: Enforcement cost, delay, support, and alternative routes

arrows.evidence: The official FWC page explicitly reports that the company paid the compensation but still did not reinstate the worker
arrows.counterexample: Payment receipt can coexist with failure to restore the job or relationship
arrows.remaining_gap: Payment instrument, net amount, timing, worker confirmation, and later recovery

arrows.evidence: The FWC account reports a further $15,045 award plus interest and a $10,000 penalty after the enforcement proceeding
arrows.counterexample: Additional monetary relief does not establish restored employment or household recovery
arrows.remaining_gap: Actual receipt of further awards, tax/net amount, and later work

arrows.to: durable recovery, trust, recurrence, or exit
arrows.evidence: The official institutional follow-up ends at payment, failed reinstatement, further award, and penalty
arrows.counterexample: Successful payment enforcement can coexist with unrecovered work, changed trust, or continued vulnerability
arrows.remaining_gap: Later employment, household recovery, trust, recurrence, collective action, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger adds the first retained official follow-up that explicitly reports a compensation payment. It demonstrates monetary remedy implementation without reinstatement or proven lived recovery; it is not a prevalence estimate and does not close the later household, trust, recurrence, or exit stages.
storage_boundary: No claimant file, payment instrument, direct personal data beyond the public case reference, or bulk archive is retained; only the bounded official institutional summary, remedy sequence, uncertainty, and open downstream arrows are represented.
